title: Micro OKR trajectory notebook — Hemant Rao
body:
Context and intent:
- Short, iterative personal notebook to keep tiny OKRs (2–4 week cadence) aligned to team priorities. Not meant to be public but useful to copy into 1:1 notes and team syncs.

Quarter micro-objective (4 weeks):
Objective: Reduce 95th-percentile inference tail for long-sequence requests and keep cost stable.
Key results (measurable):
- KR1: Decrease 95p latency for 4k-8k token requests by 18% on staging by end of cycle.
- KR2: Ship a per-model batching heuristic for long sequences that doesn't increase median latency >5%.
- KR3: Add two automated regression checks in CI for KV-cache correctness across quantized variants.

Why this matters to me:
- Directly tied to customer incidents we saw in Jan (long-request tail spikes).
- Good domain for mentoring interns (small infra + clear acceptance criteria).

Weekly check-in template (use every Monday morning):
- Wins last week: short bullets.
- Blockers: clear, who can help.
- Metrics delta (numbers).
- Action items this week (owner + ETA).

Snapshot: week-of 2026-03-09
- Wins:
  - Prototype batching heuristic merged to my feature branch (perf + correctness tests passing locally).
  - Mentored Raj on writing a KV-cache unit test; he shipped the first test.
- Blockers:
  - Reproducer for rare 95p spike still flaky in CI (only reproduces when combined with quantized path).
  - Need compute time to run larger simulation (requesting 4h on dedicated cluster).
- Metrics (staging):
  - baseline 95p for 4k-8k tokens: 1.42s -> current branch 1.20s (15% improvement, aiming for 18%).
  - median unchanged (0.23s).
- Action items:
  - AH: schedule 4h simulation on dedicated cluster (owner: me — target Tue 2026-03-10).
  - AH: pair with SRE to collect more CI artifacts when spike occurs (owner: Luis — target Wed 2026-03-11).
  - AH: add deterministic seed to quantized runner to make reproducer stable (owner: me — target Fri 2026-03-13).

Retro notes (what I learned):
- Small experiments win. The batching heuristic was straightforward but needed an explicit fallback (too aggressive batching increased latency for short requests).
- Mentoring accelerates test coverage; pair-programming was faster than asynchronous reviews for the KV test.
- CI flakiness is the main tempo limiter — invest in better observability for failing runs.

Unresolved questions / hypothesis log:
- Hypothesis A: The quantized kernel's memory allocation pattern interacts with batching to cause occasional GC-like pauses. Test: run profiler on long-run quantized workload.
- Hypothesis B: Sampling of real request sequences in replay harness is biased; need to augment with synthetic long-prefix traces from customer traces (requires privacy review).

Personal development goals this cycle (micro):
- PR cadence: get to 2 meaningful PRs merged per week (definition: >1 moderate change with tests).
- Mentorship: formally pair with one new hire/intern for at least 3 sessions.
- Communication: write a short 1-page summary for the team demo explaining the batching heuristic + failure modes.

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- Draft for the 1-pager: "Problem, intuition, simple diagrams (before/after), perf table, known caveats, next steps".
- Slack ping template for SRE: "Hey — seeing flaky 95p spikes on quantized-long workloads in CI. Can we get extended traces + perf counters? Attaching run IDs: run-20260307-09, run-20260308-14".
- Quick checklist before demo: verify fallback config, demo script with short and long request, have rollback branch ready.

Small wins log (for morale):
- 2026-02-12: first green run with new batching on 8k tokens.
- 2026-02-25: Raj's KV test caught an off-by-one that would have landed in prod.

Action backlog (prioritized, rough):
- P0: stabilize CI reproducer and add logging (blocks KR1).
- P1: land batching heuristic and toggle flag behind runtime config.
- P2: run extended perf simulation on dedicated cluster and collect traces.
- P3: write 1-pager and share in Friday demo.

To iterate next Monday:
- Update metrics snapshot with simulation numbers.
- Confirm mentorship schedule.
- Close small follow-ups (flip feature flag if safe).

Quick links I want nearby when editing:
- Confluence: inference/perf-long-seq (CONFLUENCE-1234)
- GH PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8921
- Jira: INF-5312 (CI flakiness)

End of notebook entry.
(Notes deliberately granular so copying into 1:1 is trivial.)
